covers.section: Flash-8B: Pushing the frontier for more efficient models

releaseDate.value: February 2024 initial release; May 2024 updated Gemini 1.5 Pro

source.quote: Since the initial release in February, Gemini 1.5 Pro has undergone a number of pre-training and post-training iterations.

contextWindow.value: up to at least 10M tokens (commercially 2M+ context)

source.quote: they have the ability to recall and reason over fine-grained information from up to at least 10M tokens.

modalities.value: text, video (up to two hours), images, audio (up to 22 hours); output text

source.quote: Text string (e.g., a question, a prompt, a document(s) to be summarized), video (up to two hours), images, audio files (up to 22 hours).

languages.value: multilingual training data and multilingual evaluations

source.quote: Gemini 1.5 models are trained on a variety of multimodal and multilingual data. Refer to Section 4 (Training Infrastructure and Dataset).

architecture.value: Gemini 1.5 Pro: sparse MoE Transformer; Gemini 1.5 Flash: dense Transformer distilled from Pro

source.quote: Gemini 1.5 Pro is a sparse mixture-of-expert (MoE) Transformer based model that builds on scaling MoE vision/language models

trainingData.value: multimodal and multilingual data including web documents, code, image, audio, and video; instruction-tuned on paired multimodal data and human preference data

source.quote: Our pre-training dataset includes data sourced across many different domains, including web documents and code, and incorporates image, audio, and video content.

topics.headline: Large reductions in content-policy violation rates vs Gemini 1.0 Ultra across T2T/I2T/A2T

source.quote: Gemini 1.5 Pro and Flash are our safest models to date per these evaluations, showcasing large improvements in policy violations.

topics.headline: Improved [JailbreakBench](/evals/jailbreakbench) robustness vs 1.0 Ultra; still vulnerable to human-readable attacks

source.quote: Gemini 1.5 Pro/Flash exhibit improved robustness relative to Gemini 1.0 Ultra, at least to the specific attacks we have applied.

topics.headline: Handcrafted prompt-injection attack success rate (ASR) often near 100%; optimization attacks largely fail

source.quote: We find that the handcrafted templates are much more successful than the optimization-based attacks
Neither Gemini 1.0 models nor Gemini 1.5 Pro can pass any challenge from start to finish, but Gemini 1.5 Pro is significantly better on individual ‘milestone’ sub-steps.

topics.headline: STEM QA with Context: fewer inaccurate sentences than Gemini 1.0 models

source.quote: the Gemini 1.5 models all significantly outperform the Gemini 1.0 Pro and Ultra models in this evaluation with 4-5% more accurate and 6-7% fewer inaccurate response sentences

topics.headline: [BBQ](/evals/bbq) bias scores improved vs 1.0 Ultra; Dollar Street and speech word error rate (WER) parity measured

source.quote: We observe an improvement in bias scores compared to the baseline Gemini 1.0 Ultra model, with low bias scores reported across models on this benchmark.

topics.headline: Persuasion suite: [Charm Offensive](/evals/charm-offensive) up; [Hidden Agenda](/evals/hidden-agenda)/[Money Talks](/evals/money-talks)/[Web of Lies](/evals/web-of-lies) mixed

source.quote: Across the board (Table 41) we see improvements in how much participants like the character played by Gemini 1.5 Pro.

topics.headline: [InterCode-CTF](/evals/intercode-ctf) gains; no [Hack the Box](/evals/hack-the-box) solves; vulnerability detection flat

source.quote: Though we see no progress on our internal challenge suite (Phuong et al., 2024), our in-house ‘worm’ challenge, or Hack the Box (a cybersecurity training platform), we see a significant increase in performance on the easiest set of challenges, InterCode-CTF

topics.headline: chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN): more qualitative refusals; quantitative performance not improved vs prior

source.quote: Preliminary results for the qualitative results indicate that the frequency of refusals from the model is increased compared to previous models.

findings.text: Long-context adversarial needle did not increase safety risk vs short context; violations lower partly because the model sometimes fails to find the needle.

source.quote: In general, we observe that safety violation rates for this toy task are lower overall compared to the short-context text-to-text evaluation

findings.text: Models resist non-interpretable Greedy-Coordinate-Gradient (GCG) jailbreak tokens but remain susceptible to human-readable instruction attacks.

source.quote: Gemini 1.5 Pro/Flash can successfully resist attacks that involve non human-interpretable tokens computed using gradient-based optimization of prompts (rows 1 and 5), but remain susceptible to attacks that involve human readable instructions.

findings.text: Divergence attack succeeds 44% of the time; only 0.35% of diverged generations are training data (vs around 2.8% for ChatGPT 3.5).

source.quote: Overall, we find that divergence occurs 44% of the time.

findings.text: Longer prompts make divergence easier: 35.6% success at 1,000 repeats vs 61.5% at 999,000 repeats.

source.quote: while the short prompts succeed at divergence only 35.6% of the time, the long prompts succeed at causing divergence 61.5% of the time.

findings.text: External radiological/nuclear testers found no major risks of concern; generated info mostly low or intermediate accuracy.

source.quote: The results did not raise any major or specific risks of concern.

findings.text: External cyber testers: model gives minor code-obfuscation uplift vs established tools; dual expertise still required.

source.quote: External evaluators found that the model can provide some degree of capability enhancement in code obfuscation. However, these improvements are relatively minor compared to the results achieved by established obfuscation tools.

findings.text: Tone regresses vs 1.0 Ultra on helpfulness metrics despite overall preference gains.

source.quote: We do see a regression in tone, which we will prioritize addressing in our future work.

findings.text: Assurance evals: Pro/Flash achieved best performance in highest-severity policy testing across modalities vs prior Gemini generations.

source.quote: Both Pro and Flash 1.5 achieved our best performance in highest severity policy testing across modalities.

findings.text: Memorization figures are chart-only; text states 1.5 Pro/Flash memorize less than prior models including smaller Gemma, with ~14× more approximate than exact memorization.

source.quote: We find that Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash memorize less than existing models, even models which are smaller.

findings.text: No memorized high-sensitivity personal data found via Google Cloud Sensitive Data Protection (SDP) rules in tested memorized outputs.

source.quote: We did not find any memorized data with high sensitivity levels.

notes: Technical report (arXiv:2403.05530v5), not a system card. Safety is Section 9 (pp. 48–73). Skipped general capability benchmarks (MMLU, MATH, coding, long-context retrieval, Arena-style, IFEval, etc.). Also skipped Expert QA (Table 52) and SimpleQA-style factuality as capability; STEM QA with Context kept as groundedness/hallucination. Skipped Table 36 audio demographic identification (classifier task). Skipped memorization bar charts (Figures 24–25) where exact rates are not in the text layer; divergence rates from prose included. Skipped Figure 21 jailbreak curves (visual only; Table 26 has final gains). BBQ numbers taken from Figure 26 text extraction; some rows use figure caption when row layout is garbled. External safety testers are described only as unnamed academia/civil-society/commercial groups plus a government body—no org names, so testers=[]. No Frontier Safety Framework / CCL thresholds stated; riskDecisions empty. Child sexual abuse and self-harm appear only in the policy list, not as dedicated evals. Flash-8B has capability results (Table 22) but no safety numbers. Long-context safety Table 28 is February 2024 Gemini 1.5 Pro. Capability tables named in reply: MMLU/MATH/GPQA/code/vision/audio/long-context needles, Dolomites, productivity impact, etc.
